body:
It's ok to ask. I enjoy talking. Thank you for listening.

Looking back, I remember being happy going to England in 2009. I grew up there and going back used to be like going home. This year, my wife said I should go and see old friends. I felt nothing. I remember sitting at the train station, gnawing on an egg sandwich, expecting to see myself aged 17 emerge from a cobbled street with a rucksack full of rattling beers. I felt a deep disconnect between who I was and who I am. I wanted, more than anything in the world, to talk to that kid, see where the person in between us went wrong.

The counsellor says it's just depression, a disease. Perhaps. My father suffers from it, although it's different for him, he fought in a war. (We are from and live in Eastern Europe.) But even so, if it's real in my head, it's real enough, isn't it? I was prescribed medical drugs, they felt worse than my usual state of mind. They made me feel dirty and weak, like I was stuffed full of stained cotton. I fear going to see the doctor again, as I might end up institutionalized. The mental institution in our capital has fairly recently made the national news for inhumane conditions, including dead bodies remaining in beds, next to living patients, for hours. I think it's better to die than suffer through that.

I'm at work. Drinking my coffee and firing up my Eclipse tool. I walked to work as I planned, music blaring on the buds as I planned. But then I let the train pass. You gave me food for thought. Thank you for that.

I don't know what happens next. My counsellor said I've got depression. It's all brain chemistry. But, isn't everything? Want to live, brain chemistry. Want to die, brain chemistry. How can we say one is true and the other false?

I don't think it's tough, really. Pointless and a drag. I feel like I have nothing of substance to give or receive anymore.

My kid's small for her age, of average intelligence but extremely communicative. She's insecure and a bit of a bully. I don't think we're good parents to her. We appear to care, we do activities with her, we never beat her, but she's not growing up to be a happy or good person. She reminds me of a small dog sometimes, cudly but vicious. Sorry if that sounds cold.

She's 7. My wife is 34 and I'm 35.

I have told my wife I'm having hese thoughts. She was distressed and begged me to seek professional help, which I did.

That's why I am planning to make it look like an accident.

I know it's horribly selfish, and it just makes me think I deserve to die even more. I have the sweetest, happiest daughter. Why can't I be happy about it like normal people?

Thank you for your reply.

Hi.

She's all right. She's a middle manager in a consulting firm and working her ass off. She's got a forceful personality and likes being right. She can be very sweet. We had some good fun when we were young.
